node.criteria: Pass if the mug and headphones are identifiable and their relative positions can be judged; fail if the image clearly shows either is absent or the comparison is impossible; unknown if visibility or identification is inconclusive.
node.binding: Use only the image to identify the mug and headphones and assess whether their relative placement is observable. This establishes evidence availability, not fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

Thus the requested move has progressed, but the image does not clearly establish that the original mug was moved, which is consistent with partial rather than complete fulfillment. Make the node compare the same target across source and edited snapshots, using stable visual identity/appearance and position, and distinguish a completed move from a newly added duplicate or an unresolved identity. Preserve the rubric’s partial and unknown outcomes: do not infer no progress from ambiguity, or completion from the right-side relation alone. The source shows a distinctive blue mug left of the headphones; the edit appears to retain a mug-like object on the left and shows a different-looking mug on the right, so the endpoint relation alone does not establish completion. Keep partial when there is evidence of progress but continuity/completion is unclear, and unknown when the required identity or movement evidence cannot be resolved; do not turn ambiguity into either no progress or a confident pass.
